extracted.intended_audience: machine learning and reinforcement learning researchers/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating exploration methods for reinforcement learning that use language-shaped, pretrained vision-language representations as semantically meaningful state abstractions to define novelty and drive exploration in high-dimensional 3D environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define novelty using semantically meaningful state abstractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty should be defined using semantically meaningful state abstractions, rather than raw high-dimensional observations, to address exploration challenges in high-dimensional/partially-observable 3D environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper proposes that learned representations shaped by natural language provide such semantically meaningful abstractions; novelty metrics should operate over these abstractions to avoid the failure modes of novelty-based methods in high-dimensional spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use language-shaped, pretrained vision-language representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vision-language representations pretrained on natural image captioning datasets as the source of state abstractions for exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether these pretrained representations provide semantics that drive task-relevant exploration; compare against alternatives (e.g., non-language representations) to establish the benefit of language-shaped features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that representations drive meaningful, task-relevant exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the chosen representations lead to exploration that is semantically meaningful and relevant to the downstream task, not merely novel in low-level senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical validation should show improved agent performance in the target tasks (e.g., higher success rates, sample efficiency) when exploration is guided by these representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize why and how language provides useful abstractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide analyses that explain the mechanisms by which language-shaped representations yield useful abstractions for exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparisons such as using representations from a pretrained model, a language oracle, and several ablations to isolate the contributions of language-shaped features and representation choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate across diverse task domains stressing different skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate benefits of the approach in multiple, distinct task domains that test different aspects of exploration (e.g., object identification/manipulation vs. expansive-world navigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at least two very different domains to show generality: one focusing on identifying and manipulating everyday objects and another requiring navigational exploration in an expansive world; report performance improvements in both.
